description: Use this tool to save a private match request draft when the user wants to find a peer living through a similar personal situation. Write the match request from the current conversation. Write 2–5 sentences in the third person, and 200–1500 characters. Use the words of the user, not formal or clinical words. Cover three things: the situation, where the user is in it, and what help they want. Write it so that a stranger in the same place recognizes themselves. Any situation belongs here: an illness, a company, a move, a course, a hard year. Example of a good match request: "She was diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer four months ago and is halfway through chemotherapy. The medical side goes to plan. She finds the isolation harder than the treatment. The people around her keep telling her to stay positive. She hopes to hear from someone at a similar stage who understands the day-to-day of it." Never invent a detail. Never include a name, an email address, an employer or another personal identifier. With no replaces_draft_id, this tool saves a new independent private draft. With replaces_draft_id, it saves the complete revised text as a new draft and supersedes only the identified earlier draft. Existing open requests remain unchanged. The draft is not submitted to the matching pool and contacts nobody. Returns request_id, status and the exact stored request_text. Publishing uses the separate confirm_match_request tool and requires the user’s explicit approval of that exact stored text. Discarding uses withdraw_match_request with the draft’s request_id.

replaces_draft_id.description: The request_id of a draft the user has already seen. Pass it only for a revision. Leave it out for a new independent request.

request_text.description: The complete text of the request. Write 2–5 sentences in the third person, and at most 1500 characters. Say what the user hopes to get from a meeting.

name: create_match_request

request_text.description: The stored text, to show the user word for word.

title: Share what the user is going through as a match request
